author: tugtugboat
quote: Thirteen years after GTA V, the last thing I expected to be thinking during a shootout was how much better it would feel at 60 fps. GTA VI looks great, but even on PS5 Pro, that 30 fps cap is rough. When the frame rate dips in the middle of a fight, I feel it the moment I try to swing my aim onto the next target. For a game that asks me to spend this much time shooting, at $80 before tax, that’s a big letdown.What bothered me most was what counted toward the good ending. Give me a reason to care about the relationship, sure. But after a whole game of stealing cars and pulling guns, why does my shot at the best outcome hinge on a relationship meter and a body count? I’d have loved an ending where a heist I pulled off especially well, or a job I completely botched, came back to matter. That would’ve made the ending feel like it belonged to my playthrough.Then there’s the selective realism. I have to remember to eat, get gas and work out, but I can take half a dozen rounds from the cops, pop a pill and keep moving. If I can shrug **** that easily, why is running low on gas the part where the game insists I take reality seriously? By the end, I was tired of looking after my character and still wanted more say in what actually happened to them. That’s a disappointing place to land after a thirteen-year wait.
